sections.title: How the deck wins
sections.text: Kilo does not win alone: it multiplies. Every time it taps, it proliferates, and the deck taps it once or twice a round without attacking: Relic of Legends, the station of Inspirit or of Uthros Research Craft, waterbend and improvise; North Pole Patrol untaps it for a second tap. Those proliferates grow the counters on some twenty rocks, engines and creatures, and the counters turn into mana, cards and removal. It wins with the first finisher that arrives against the whole table: Darksteel Reactor with 20 charge counters, Lux Artillery dealing 10 to each rival in your end step with 30 counters on the table, or the loop Lux Artillery + Crystalline Crawler + Meticulous Excavation finished with Reckless Fireweaver. Plan B: the same board attacks with Cyberdrive Awakener, Kappa Cannoneer and Alibou's trigger. The realistic line: Kilo on turn 3 in 4 of every 5 games, the engine running on turns 4 to 6, and the win around turns 10 to 12 (turn 8 if Solar Array finds Darksteel Reactor early). There is no tutor for the Reactor or the Artillery: the deck draws a lot and wins with whichever finisher arrives.

sections.title: Mulligan
sections.text: Keep 3 to 5 lands, or 2 if you have Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Pentad Prism, Everflowing Chalice, Barrels of Blasting Jelly or Chromatic Star, as long as the hand does something by turn 3. Kilo needs {U}{R}{W}: a two-color hand with no Arcane Signet, Command Tower, Mystic Monastery, Path of Ancestry or other source of any color is a mulligan. Almost any hand with good lands is a keep if it has Sol Ring, Solar Array, Insight Engine, Surge Conductor, Inspirit or Pentad Prism. Mulligan with 0 to 1 lands, with 6 or more, and with 2 lands and no cheap mana. Don't keep a hand just because it has Darksteel Reactor or Lux Artillery: without an engine they arrive late. With the free mulligan you keep seven cards in about 9 of every 10 games.

sections.title: Turn by turn
sections.text: T1: a tapped land of three colors (Mystic Monastery, Path of Ancestry) or Rustvale Bridge, plus Sol Ring, Barrels of Blasting Jelly or Chromatic Star if you have them. T2: Arcane Signet, Pentad Prism paid with two colors, Everflowing Chalice with a multikicker payment, a piece that puts counters (Hangarback Walker with X=1, Coretapper, Steel Overseer), or a two-drop that pushes the artifact plan (Enthusiastic Mechanaut makes them cost {1} less; Reckless Fireweaver deals 1 damage to each opponent whenever an artifact enters). T3: Kilo, and tap him that same turn if you can (he has haste). T4 to T6: one engine per turn (Solar Array, Relic of Legends, Insight Engine, Surge Conductor, Inspirit, Uthros Research Craft, Tekuthal, Empowered Autogenerator) and Kilo taps at home. T6 to T9: Darksteel Reactor or Lux Artillery with {1}{U} open for Negate, Solar Array on your best artifact each turn, and Insight Engine at the end of the turn of the opponent who plays before you. In each proliferate choose everything of yours that has counters: the Reactor, the rocks (Everflowing Chalice, Pentad Prism, Astral Cornucopia, Empowered Autogenerator), Insight Engine, Lux Cannon, Titan Forge, Inspirit and Uthros Research Craft, the creatures with +1/+1 counters and the Incubators, and the stun counters you put with Tranquilize.

sections.title: When to cast Kilo
sections.text: On turn 3 almost always: with Arcane Signet, Command Tower, a three-color land or the Barrels, he comes down on time in 4 of every 5 games. Exception: if there are no counters on the table yet and you have Insight Engine or Solar Array, cast the engine first and Kilo on turn 4. He has haste, so tap him the same turn: Relic of Legends, a station, or an attack into a table with no blockers. If they kill him, recast him for 5 (then 7) the next turn; he taps that same turn, so losing Kilo costs you a turn, not the plan. With Lux Artillery on the table, recasting him paid with three colors leaves him as a 6/6. To save him: Airbending Lesson on himself (you recast him for {2} from exile), Ripples of Potential if he already has a counter, or Meticulous Excavation on your turn to return him to hand and cast him without tax.

sections.title: When to attack and when to wait
sections.text: Kilo does not need to attack: tap him at home to pay costs and leave him as a blocker. Attack only a rival with no blockers or with smaller ones: the attack also proliferates, loads Long-Range Sensor and fires Alibou. To load the Sensor, attack with a flyer (Enthusiastic Mechanaut, Chrome Host Seedshark, Tekuthal, Thought Monitor) at the rival with no flyers. With Alibou on the table, tap your rocks for your spells first and then attack with any artifact creature: the X damage kills the blocker before blockers are declared. Kappa Cannoneer attacks the turn another artifact enters, because that turn it is unblockable. Never attack into a wide board of tokens; save the full attack for the turn of Cyberdrive Awakener. Your main finishers (Darksteel Reactor, Lux Artillery, Reckless Fireweaver) don't need combat.

sections.title: Tutors and what to look for
sections.text: The only tutor is Trophy Mage (an artifact with mana value 3). Early, look for Solar Array (Darksteel Reactor and Lux Cannon enter loaded) or Relic of Legends (more taps for Kilo); with the engine running, Insight Engine or Surge Conductor; if a rival plays artifact sweepers, Inspirit. Meticulous Excavation returns Trophy Mage to hand for a second search. Long-Range Sensor discovers 4 and can give you Darksteel Reactor, Lux Artillery or Crystalline Crawler for free. The rest of the access to the finishers is card draw: Insight Engine, Uthros Research Craft, Jhoira, Waterbending Lesson, Thirst for Knowledge, Universal Surveillance and Etched Oracle. The Mycosynth Gardens and Phyrexian Metamorph copy Lux Artillery once it is on the table.

sections.title: Graveyard
sections.text: The graveyard is support, not the plan: no route needs it. Emry is the engine: each turn she recasts from the graveyard Chromatic Star or Soul-Guide Lantern (one card for one mana), or a finisher that was destroyed, countered or discarded to Thirst for Knowledge. Her mill of 4 on entering can send a key piece to the graveyard: get it back with the same Emry. Starfall Invocation with the promised gift returns a creature of yours that died in the sweep (Kilo if you let him go to the graveyard, Tekuthal or Alibou). Against rival graveyards, Soul-Guide Lantern exiles a card when it enters, or every rival graveyard when sacrificed: save it for a reanimator or a card with escape or flashback.

sections.title: What to protect against
sections.text: What hurts most: artifact sweepers (Vandalblast, Farewell, Austere Command), the exile or bounce of the Reactor (it is indestructible, so destroying it is not enough), a counterspell on the Reactor or Lux Artillery, effects that shut off artifact abilities, and fast combos on turns 5 to 6. Against an artifact sweeper, in order: Negate; Ripples of Potential in response (everything that gets a counter phases out); Inspirit at 8 or more counters (your other artifacts are indestructible); Resourceful Defense moves the charge counters of what gets destroyed onto the Reactor; then Emry and Kilo rebuild with haste. Cast the Reactor or Lux Artillery only with {1}{U} open, and bait first with a card-draw spell. Commit what wins within two turns, and keep a finisher in hand if two rivals can sweep.

sections.title: Removal priorities
sections.text: First whatever wins or shuts you down: combo pieces (Swords to Plowshares, Dispatch, Fateful Absence and Volt Charge are instants, usable on the rival's turn) and the anti-artifact or enchantment pieces that slow you (Chaos Warp, Airbending Lesson, Lux Cannon). Then the commander that hits hardest: Swords to Plowshares, Chaos Warp, or Tranquilize, which Kilo keeps adding stun counters to without the commander returning to the command zone. Then the flyers that attack you and the blockers that stop your attacks, with Alibou's trigger and Barrels of Blasting Jelly. Keep Swords to Plowshares and Chaos Warp for real threats, and use Volt Charge on small things, because it also proliferates. Aim Tranquilize, Chaos Warp and Alibou's trigger at the table's leader before using them only for yourself. Keep Negate for sweepers and for your winning turn.

sections.title: When to clear the board
sections.text: Organic Extinction when the rivals have more nonartifact creatures than you: pay almost all of it with improvise (tapping artifacts and Kilo, who proliferates) and your artifact creatures survive. You lose Tekuthal, Jhoira, Reckless Fireweaver, Emry, Trophy Mage, North Pole Patrol, Chrome Host Seedshark and Deepglow Skate: use it when the table loses more than you. Starfall Invocation destroys everything, Kilo included: use it only when you're losing on creatures, promise the gift to the least dangerous rival and recover Kilo, Tekuthal or Alibou. Before a sweep, activate Tekuthal to make it indestructible, move counters onto the Reactor with Moxite Refinery, and if Resourceful Defense is on the table, the counters of what dies move to a permanent that survives (all of them count for Lux Artillery). Hangarback Walker leaves a flying Thopter when it dies. The Reactor, the Artillery and your rocks survive both sweepers: your plan stays on.

combos.title: Darksteel Reactor to 20 counters
combos.meta: Alternate win · Reactor + a funnel (Moxite Refinery, Resourceful Defense or Deepglow Skate) · {4}, then 2 to 7 mana
combos.text:
Needs: Darksteel Reactor on the battlefield; repeated proliferate (Kilo, Surge Conductor, Tekuthal); a funnel; {1}{U} open to Negate on the turn it reaches 20.
Tap Solar Array and cast Darksteel Reactor paying {4} with four colors (black or green from Pentad Prism, Relic of Legends or Astral Cornucopia): it enters with 4 charge counters.
At each upkeep accept its counter; with Strionic Resonator ({2}) copy that trigger while it's on the stack: +2 per turn.
Each proliferate adds 1 (2 with Tekuthal): Kilo tapping, Surge Conductor, Tezzeret's Gambit, Experimental Augury, Volt Charge, Karn's Bastion. Inspirit puts 2 charge counters on it at the beginning of each of your combats.
Moxite Refinery (your main phase, {2}): remove X counters from Crystalline Crawler, Hangarback Walker, Empowered Autogenerator, Titan Forge or an Incubator and put them on the Reactor as charge counters.
Resourceful Defense ({4}{W}, instant speed): at the end of the turn of the rival before you, move the counters of Empowered Autogenerator, Titan Forge, Lux Cannon or Insight Engine to the Reactor.
When it reaches 20 you win right then, even on another player's turn: you don't wait for upkeep.
If a rival tries to exile or bounce the Reactor at 19 (18 with Tekuthal), respond with an instant proliferate (Kilo tapped with Relic of Legends, Experimental Augury, Volt Charge, Ripples of Potential): the winning trigger resolves before their removal.

combos.title: Deepglow Skate + Strionic Resonator on the Reactor
combos.meta: Reactor from 5 to 20 in one spell · Reactor + Deepglow Skate + Strionic Resonator · {4}{U} + {2}
combos.text:
Needs: Darksteel Reactor with 5 or more charge counters (10 without the Resonator); Deepglow Skate in hand; Strionic Resonator untapped; {4}{U} + {2}.
Cast Deepglow Skate with Negate or Ripples of Potential open if you can.
When it enters, its trigger targets the Reactor and all your permanents with counters (Empowered Autogenerator, Insight Engine, Lux Cannon, Inspirit).
With the trigger on the stack (you get priority first), activate the Resonator ({2}) and copy the trigger with the same targets.
The copy resolves: the Reactor goes from 5 to 10. The original resolves: from 10 to 20, and you win.
Without the Resonator, Lithoform Engine ({2}) copies the trigger just the same. Later, Meticulous Excavation returns Deepglow Skate to your hand so you can repeat it.

combos.title: Lux Artillery in your end step
combos.meta: 10 damage to each rival per trigger · Lux Artillery + 30 counters · 0 mana; {2} per copy
combos.text:
Needs: Lux Artillery on the battlefield; 30 or more counters of any kind among your artifacts and creatures (charge, +1/+1, Incubators) when your end step begins, and again on resolution.
In your second main phase count the counters: Darksteel Reactor, Everflowing Chalice, Empowered Autogenerator, Inspirit, Uthros Research Craft, Lux Cannon, the creatures with +1/+1 counters and the Incubators. If they are short, proliferate (Kilo with Relic of Legends, Karn's Bastion for {4}).
Don't spend counters from Crystalline Crawler, Pentad Prism or Etched Oracle in the end step: the condition is checked on resolution.
It triggers at the beginning of your end step. With the trigger on the stack, before passing priority, activate Strionic Resonator ({2}) and Lithoform Engine ({2}) to copy it: 20 or 30 damage to each rival.
Second Artillery: Phyrexian Metamorph copying Lux Artillery, or The Mycosynth Gardens ({4}, tap) turned into a copy; each one triggers separately and can be copied.
With two Artilleries, the Resonator and the Lithoform Engine make it 40 to each rival in a single end step.

combos.title: Lux Artillery + Crystalline Crawler + Meticulous Excavation
combos.meta: Unlimited mana and artifact entries (the line Commander Salt sees) · 3 cards + 1 finisher · {4} in four colors + {2}{W} per loop
combos.text:
Needs: Lux Artillery and Meticulous Excavation on the battlefield; Crystalline Crawler in hand; your turn, in a main phase; a black or green source for the first cast (Pentad Prism, Relic of Legends, Solar Array, Astral Cornucopia, Barrels of Blasting Jelly, Chromatic Star, Spire of Industry, The Mycosynth Gardens, Empowered Autogenerator or Exotic Orchard); Enthusiastic Mechanaut off the battlefield (with her in play each loop nets 0 mana); a finisher on the battlefield: Reckless Fireweaver, Surge Conductor with Darksteel Reactor, or Etched Oracle within reach.
Cast Crystalline Crawler paying {4} with four different colors: white, blue, red and black or green. Converge and Lux Artillery's sunburst give it 4 + 4 = 8 +1/+1 counters.
Remove the 8 counters as mana, choosing colors: {W} and two more for Meticulous Excavation, and white, blue, red and black or green to recast Crystalline Crawler. You have 1 left over. Take the mana BEFORE activating Meticulous Excavation: that way a removal spell in response takes nothing from you.
Activate Meticulous Excavation ({2}{W}) on Crystalline Crawler: it returns to your hand. You don't need to hold priority: everything happens in the same main phase, and floating mana is lost when the phase changes.
Recast Crystalline Crawler with four colors: it enters again with 8. Each loop adds 1 mana, one artifact spell cast and one artifact entry.
Finisher: Reckless Fireweaver deals 1 damage to each rival per entry (unlimited damage); Surge Conductor proliferates per entry and takes Darksteel Reactor to 20 by itself; with spare mana, Meticulous Excavation returns Etched Oracle, you recast it with four colors (8 counters) and activate it targeting each rival until they draw from an empty library.
Jhoira and Uthros Research Craft make you draw on each loop: stop the loop before emptying your library. Kappa Cannoneer grows +1 and becomes unblockable with each entry if you loop before combat (it can kill only one rival).

combos.title: Cyberdrive Awakener + Alibou: all-in attack
combos.meta: Flying attack from the whole board · Cyberdrive Awakener + 8 or more noncreature artifacts (Alibou for haste and damage) · {5}{U} paid with lands
combos.text:
Needs: 8 or more noncreature artifacts untapped (rocks, Darksteel Reactor, Lux Artillery, Incubators, artifact lands); {5}{U} from lands that are not artifacts; best with Alibou and Steel Overseer on the battlefield.
In your precombat main phase pay for Cyberdrive Awakener with non-artifact lands only: rocks and artifact lands tapped for mana could not attack.
When it enters, each noncreature artifact you control becomes a 4/4 until end of turn, and all your artifact creatures fly. Those on the battlefield since the start of the turn can attack; the ones that entered this turn, and Awakener itself, need Alibou's haste.
Tap Steel Overseer: +1/+1 on each artifact creature.
Attack with everything and with Kilo (he proliferates when he taps: one more +1/+1 counter on each attacker that already has one). Alibou's trigger counts all the tapped artifacts, attackers included: X damage to the flying blocker that bothers you or directly to a rival. With Strionic Resonator, copy that trigger.
With Inspirit at 8 or more, your attacking artifacts are indestructible. If you don't kill, remember the rocks go back to being noncreature artifacts at the end of the turn.

cards.Kilo, Apogee Mind: Your multiplier: it proliferates every time it taps. Tap him with costs, not by attacking: Inspirit's or Uthros Research Craft's station, Relic of Legends, waterbend and improvise; North Pole Patrol untaps him for a second tap, and Strionic Resonator copies the trigger. Leave him home as a blocker and tap him with Relic of Legends at the end of the turn of the opponent who plays before you.
cards.Sol Ring: Turn 1 always: on turn 2 cast a rock or an engine of 3 (Solar Array, Insight Engine). Late, it pays the X of Universal Surveillance and for Insight Engine; North Pole Patrol untaps it for two more mana.
cards.Arcane Signet: Turn 2: it gives any of Kilo's three colors and secures his turn 3. It doesn't give black or green: for Crystalline Crawler and Etched Oracle use other sources.
cards.Everflowing Chalice: Turn 2 with a multikicker payment; each proliferate from Kilo adds one mana permanently. With Solar Array tapped first, two payments with four colors leave it with six counters.
cards.Pentad Prism: Turn 2, paid with two colors. Spend one counter but always leave at least one so Kilo can refill it. Its mana can be black or green: your fourth color for Crystalline Crawler and Etched Oracle.
cards.Relic of Legends: The piece that taps Kilo the most: tap him for one mana at any time, and he proliferates. Do it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you (he has been blocking through the round and untaps right away) or in response to a removal spell. It also taps Tekuthal, Jhoira, Emry or Alibou for mana, and gives black or green for Crystalline Crawler.
cards.Commander's Sphere: Turn-4 rock with Kilo's three colors and a target for Trophy Mage. Sacrifice it for a card in response to an artifact removal spell, or when the mana is already spare.
cards.Solar Array: Tap it right before your best artifact of the turn and pay for that artifact with every color you can, black or green included: Darksteel Reactor enters with 4 charge counters, Lux Cannon is ready to fire, and Insight Engine draws four on its first activation. Use it this way every turn; target for Trophy Mage.
cards.Astral Cornucopia: Bad early. Cast it with X=1 on turn 4 after Kilo, or with X=1 through Solar Array paid with three colors (4 counters). Each proliferate adds one mana of a color, black or green included.
cards.Crystalline Crawler: Cast it with four colors (black or green from Pentad Prism, Relic of Legends or Solar Array): it enters with 4 counters, 8 with Lux Artillery. Tap it each turn for a counter, and spend the counters as mana on a big turn or move them to the Reactor with Moxite Refinery. It is the loop piece with Lux Artillery and Meticulous Excavation.
cards.Barrels of Blasting Jelly: Turn 1: once per turn it converts one mana into any color without tapping; it fixes Kilo's {U}{R}{W} and gives the fourth color to Crystalline Crawler. Since it doesn't tap, it always helps with improvise or waterbend. Late, {5} and sacrifice it: 5 damage to a creature.
cards.Chromatic Star: Turn 1, or when a color is missing: trade it for a card. With Emry it comes back every turn: one color, one card and one artifact entry (Surge Conductor proliferates, Reckless Fireweaver deals 1 to each rival, Jhoira and Uthros Research Craft draw).
cards.Enthusiastic Mechanaut: Turn 2: your artifacts cost {1} less, and it is a flyer that attacks at no risk to load Long-Range Sensor and fire Alibou. With it on the table, artifacts with sunburst or converge get one color fewer: don't cast it if you have Crystalline Crawler and Lux Artillery for the loop.
cards.Inspirit, Flagship Vessel: Station it by tapping Kilo: he proliferates first, and then as many charge counters enter as his power. From 1 counter, at the beginning of each of your combats put 2 charge counters on the Reactor or a +1/+1 counter on Kilo. Get to 8 as soon as you can (Kilo with counters, Hangarback Walker or Crystalline Crawler station more): your other artifacts become indestructible and hexproof.
cards.Uthros Research Craft: Cast it before the batch of cheap rocks and station it with a single tap of Kilo (3 power gets it to 3): from then on each artifact spell draws a card. Proliferate it so it flies at 12. Target for Trophy Mage.
cards.Insight Engine: Activate it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you, after proliferating: draw 2, 3, 4 and more each turn. North Pole Patrol untaps it for a second activation, and Lithoform Engine copies the activation. Paid through Solar Array, its first activation draws four.
cards.Coretapper: Turn 2: each turn one charge counter on Everflowing Chalice or Pentad Prism (more mana), then on the Reactor, Lux Cannon, Long-Range Sensor or Insight Engine. Put one on Kilo so Ripples of Potential can phase him out. Sacrifice it for two charge counters in response to removal, or to close out the Reactor.
cards.Steel Overseer: Tap it each turn starting the turn after you cast it: +1/+1 counter on each artifact creature, Kilo included. A bigger Kilo stations more, Lux Artillery reaches 30 sooner, and it is the engine of the attack plan.
cards.Surge Conductor: Each nontoken artifact that enters, artifact lands included, proliferates: cast it before the batch of cheap rocks. In the Crystalline Crawler loop it takes Darksteel Reactor to 20 by itself. Target for Trophy Mage.
cards.Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus: Doubles every proliferate: each Kilo tap is worth two. It costs {2}{U}{U} (two blue in a three-color deck), so it usually comes down on turn 4 or 5; meanwhile it is a 3/5 flyer that blocks. Before a destructive sweeper, remove three counters from your other permanents to make it indestructible.
cards.Hangarback Walker: Cast it with X=1 on turn 2: each proliferate and its ability ({1}, tap) grow it. Big, it stations Inspirit, pays improvise or waterbend, and its counters go to the Reactor with Moxite Refinery. If it dies it leaves one flying Thopter per counter (use markers).
cards.Long-Range Sensor: Any attack on a player puts a counter on it: one flyer attacking the player with no flyers is enough. With two counters, {1} in your main phase: discover 4, which can give you Darksteel Reactor, Lux Artillery or Crystalline Crawler for free. Always choose it when you proliferate.
cards.Etched Oracle: Cast it with four colors (black or green, from a source of any color) and draw three immediately for {1}; with three colors wait for a proliferate. With Lux Artillery it enters with eight: two activations. With the loop's unlimited mana, target each rival until they draw from an empty library.
cards.Patrolling Peacemaker: It enters with two +1/+1 counters and proliferates whenever a rival targets another player or their things: in aggressive pods that's several proliferates per round that cost you nothing. Say it out loud when it triggers. Target for Trophy Mage.
cards.Chrome Host Seedshark: Each noncreature spell leaves an Incubator with as many +1/+1 counters as its mana value: an artifact that proliferate grows, that counts for Lux Artillery, that is tapped to improvise or waterbend, and whose entry triggers Reckless Fireweaver and Kappa Cannoneer. Transform it ({2}) only if you need a body. It is a 2/4 flyer that blocks well.
cards.North Pole Patrol: From the next turn, tap it to untap Kilo after his first tap, and tap him again: two proliferates. Late, it untaps Empowered Autogenerator, Insight Engine, Lux Cannon or Sol Ring. Its waterbend ({3}, payable by tapping Kilo and artifacts) taps an attacking rival.
cards.Strionic Resonator: {2}: copies one of your triggers while it's on the stack. The best: Kilo's proliferate, Lux Artillery's end-step trigger (+10 to each rival), Deepglow Skate's trigger (quadruple), Alibou's trigger and the upkeep trigger of the Reactor. Leave {2} open on the winning turn.
cards.Lithoform Engine: Like Strionic Resonator, but it also copies activated abilities: the one of Insight Engine, Lux Cannon or Etched Oracle. With {3} it copies Tezzeret's Gambit or Waterbending Lesson; with {4} it copies Lux Artillery while it's being cast.
cards.Phyrexian Metamorph: A second copy of what pays best: Lux Artillery (two 10-damage triggers), Surge Conductor, Insight Engine or Crystalline Crawler (it also works in the loop). If you lack blue, pay 2 life. If a rival has a better artifact or creature, copy that.
cards.Darksteel Reactor: Your main win: cast it through Solar Array with four colors (it enters with 4) and with {1}{U} open for Negate. Always proliferate it, accept its counter at every upkeep, and fill it with Moxite Refinery, Resourceful Defense or Deepglow Skate. It is indestructible: it only fears exile, bounce and counterspells.
cards.Lux Artillery: Cast it early if artifact creatures are coming: each enters with a +1/+1 counter per color paid (a recast Kilo is a 6/6, Crystalline Crawler enters with 8). Your normal game takes it to 30 counters; from there it deals 10 to each rival in each of your end steps, and 20 or 30 when you copy the trigger with Strionic Resonator and Lithoform Engine.
cards.Kappa Cannoneer: Pay for it almost entirely with improvise: tap Kilo (he proliferates) and your idle rocks. Each artifact that enters, tokens included, gives it a +1/+1 counter and makes it unblockable that turn: cast a cheap artifact before attacking. It kills one rival at a time; meanwhile it is a blocker that is hard to remove.
cards.Reckless Fireweaver: Turn 2: each artifact that enters, Incubators included, deals 1 to each rival; in a game that adds up to 15 to 20. In the Crystalline Crawler loop it is the finisher: unlimited damage. Careful: Organic Extinction kills it too.
cards.Cyberdrive Awakener: Save it for the final attack turn: cast it only with non-artifact lands in your precombat main phase, with 8 or more noncreature artifacts untapped. They all become 4/4 flyers; with Alibou, those that entered that turn also attack.
cards.Alibou, Ancient Witness: Before attacking, tap your rocks for your spells; then attack with any artifact creature: X damage to any target, where X is your tapped artifacts (4 to 8 in a normal turn). It kills the blocker before blocks or burns a player. It gives haste to Kappa Cannoneer and to everything that Cyberdrive Awakener animates.
cards.Deepglow Skate: Bad early. Cast it when it doubles something that wins: Darksteel Reactor from 10 to 20 (from 5 with Strionic Resonator), Lux Artillery above 30, Empowered Autogenerator or Insight Engine. Target all your permanents with counters and the rival creature that has stun counters from Tranquilize.
cards.Resourceful Defense: Cast it before a sweeper: each permanent of yours with counters that leaves the battlefield passes its counters to another of yours (charge counters to the indestructible Reactor). Its ability ({4}{W}, instant speed) moves the charge from Empowered Autogenerator, Titan Forge or Lux Cannon to the Reactor at the end of a rival's turn, and it can win at that moment.
cards.Moxite Refinery: Only in your main phase: {2}, tap it and remove X counters from an artifact or creature you control to put X charge counters on an artifact. It moves the +1/+1 counters of Crystalline Crawler, Hangarback Walker or an Incubator to the Reactor, or fills Insight Engine (you draw that many) or Lux Cannon.
cards.Meticulous Excavation: Bad early: it is the loop piece with Crystalline Crawler and Lux Artillery. Meanwhile, on your turn, {2}{W}: return Trophy Mage, Thought Monitor, Deepglow Skate or Etched Oracle to your hand to repeat them, save a permanent of yours from removal, or return Kilo to cast him again without the tax.
cards.Tezzeret's Gambit: Two cards and a proliferate: cast it on turns 3 to 5, once there are counters on the table. Without blue, pay 2 life.
cards.Experimental Augury: On turn 2 with Everflowing Chalice or Pentad Prism on the table, or at the end of a rival's turn: you pick the missing card and proliferate. Being an instant, it takes the Reactor from 19 to 20 in response to removal.
cards.Empowered Autogenerator: It enters tapped: cast it on turn 4 or 5 and within a few turns it gives 5 to 8 mana of one color per turn (each proliferate adds). It pays for the X of Universal Surveillance, for Insight Engine, and for the black or green of Crystalline Crawler. Late, its counters go to the Reactor with Moxite Refinery or Resourceful Defense.
cards.Thirst for Knowledge: Instant: at the end of a rival's turn, draw three and discard a spare rock. With Emry on the table you can discard Darksteel Reactor or Lux Artillery and cast them from the graveyard.
cards.Waterbending Lesson: Pay the waterbend by tapping Kilo and an artifact: you draw three without discarding, and Kilo proliferates. From turn 4 it is your best draw spell.
cards.Universal Surveillance: Bad early. Late, pay {U}{U}{U} with rocks of any color and the X by tapping idle artifacts and Kilo (he proliferates); with Empowered Autogenerator it draws 6 to 10.
cards.Jhoira, Weatherlight Captain: Cast it on turn 4 or 5 before a batch of artifacts: it draws a card for each artifact or legendary you cast, which is more than a third of the deck. If you have spare mana, Relic of Legends taps her for mana. Organic Extinction kills her.
cards.Thought Monitor: With 4 to 6 artifacts it costs 1 to 3: two cards and a flying artifact that loads Long-Range Sensor. Meticulous Excavation returns it so you can draw again.
cards.Trophy Mage: Searches for an artifact with mana value 3. Early: Solar Array or Relic of Legends; with the engine running: Insight Engine or Surge Conductor; against artifact sweepers: Inspirit. It also reaches Uthros Research Craft, Long-Range Sensor, Patrolling Peacemaker, Commander's Sphere and Titan Forge.
cards.Emry, Lurker of the Loch: With several artifacts she costs {U} or nothing. From the next turn, each turn she recasts from the graveyard Chromatic Star or Soul-Guide Lantern (one card for one mana), or a finisher that was destroyed or discarded. If her mill throws a finisher away, get it back with her.
cards.Swords to Plowshares: Your best answer: for {W} and at instant speed, against the commander or the creature that beats you. Don't spend it on minor threats.
cards.Dispatch: From turn 3, with three artifacts, exile a creature for {W} at instant speed. Without metalcraft it only taps an attacker: keep it until you have the artifacts.
cards.Fateful Absence: Instant for {1}{W} against a creature or planeswalker. The Clue its controller gets matters little: use it against the table's leader.
cards.Chaos Warp: Your answer to any permanent: enchantments or artifacts that shut down your artifacts, and indestructible commanders. Use it on whatever you can't answer any other way.
cards.Airbending Lesson: Exile a nonland permanent and draw: best against tokens, permanents with counters or enter-the-battlefield effects, because the owner can cast it again for {2}. On defense, exile your own Kilo in response to removal and recast him from exile for {2}.
cards.Volt Charge: 3 damage to any target and a proliferate, all at instant speed: it kills a small creature at the end of a turn, or takes the Reactor from 19 to 20 in response to removal.
cards.Tranquilize: Shuts down the commander or the best creature of a rival without changing its zone, so it doesn't return to the command zone. Each proliferate adds a stun counter to it: as long as you keep doing that, it doesn't untap.
cards.Lux Cannon: Cast it through Solar Array with four colors: it enters with 4 counters and destroys a permanent that same turn. Afterward, tap it each turn for a counter and proliferate it to fire every one or two turns; North Pole Patrol untaps it.
cards.Titan Forge: A charge-counter battery: charge it with {3} when mana is spare, and proliferate it. With three counters, a 9/9 Golem against big creatures; late, its charge goes to the Reactor with Moxite Refinery or Resourceful Defense. Target for Trophy Mage.
cards.Negate: Save it for the winning turn or for the sweeper that takes you out of the game; it also protects the Reactor from an instant exile. Never on a minor spell.
cards.Ripples of Potential: In response to a sweeper or removal: proliferate and phase out everything that got a counter until your next turn (Kilo needs a counter first). On the winning turn it is a shield and an extra proliferate at once.
cards.Organic Extinction: Pay for it almost entirely with improvise, tapping artifacts and Kilo (he proliferates). It kills only nonartifact creatures: your artifact creatures survive, but you lose Tekuthal, Jhoira, Reckless Fireweaver and Emry. Use it when the table loses more than you.
cards.Starfall Invocation: A total board wipe for when you're losing on creatures. Promise the gift to the least dangerous rival and return your best dead creature: Kilo (if you let him go to the graveyard he comes back without tax), Tekuthal or Alibou. Your rocks, the Reactor and the Artillery are not touched.
cards.Soul-Guide Lantern: On entering it exiles the key card of a rival's graveyard. Sacrifice it to exile every rival graveyard against a reanimator, or for {1} to draw if you don't need that. Emry recasts it.
cards.Command Tower: Kilo's three colors from turn 1; it doesn't make black or green.
cards.Adarkar Wastes: White or blue, untapped for 1 life; colorless for free when you don't need color.
cards.Shivan Reef: Blue or red, untapped for 1 life; colorless for free when you don't need color.
cards.Sulfur Falls: Blue or red; it enters untapped with an Island or Mountain on the battlefield, so play it from turn 2 on.
cards.Glacial Fortress: White or blue; it enters untapped with a Plains or Island on the battlefield, so play it from turn 2 on.
cards.Clifftop Retreat: Red or white; it enters untapped with a Mountain or Plains on the battlefield, so play it from turn 2 on.
cards.Radiant Summit: Red or white; it enters untapped with two basic lands on the battlefield: save it for turn 3 or later.
cards.Rugged Prairie: Filter: with one red or white mana it gives {R}{R}, {R}{W} or {W}{W}, for Kilo, Alibou and Starfall Invocation.
cards.Cascade Bluffs: Filter: with one blue or red mana it gives {U}{U}, {U}{R} or {R}{R}, for Tekuthal and Universal Surveillance.
cards.Exotic Orchard: It gives the colors of the rivals' lands: often black or green, the fourth color for Crystalline Crawler and Etched Oracle.
cards.Spire of Industry: With an artifact on the battlefield it gives any color for 1 life, black or green included; without artifacts, only colorless.
cards.Seat of the Synod: Blue and an artifact: it counts for Dispatch, affinity and improvise, and makes Surge Conductor proliferate. It dies to artifact sweepers.
cards.Ancient Den: White and an artifact: it counts for Dispatch, affinity and improvise, and makes Surge Conductor proliferate.
cards.Great Furnace: Red and an artifact: it counts for Dispatch, affinity and improvise, and makes Surge Conductor proliferate.
cards.Rustvale Bridge: Enters tapped: play it on turn 1. Red or white, an artifact, and indestructible: it survives the sweepers that destroy.
cards.Karn's Bastion: Late, {4} and tap it: one more proliferate per turn (two with Tekuthal). Use it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you with the spare mana.
cards.The Mycosynth Gardens: Early, {1} and tap it: any color, black or green for Crystalline Crawler. Late, {4} and tap it: it becomes a second Lux Artillery; it also copies Surge Conductor or Insight Engine (X=3). Never copy Everflowing Chalice, Pentad Prism or Astral Cornucopia: their copied X is worth 0.
cards.Mystic Monastery: Enters tapped with Kilo's three colors: play it on turn 1 or 2.
cards.Path of Ancestry: Enters tapped with Kilo's three colors: play it on turn 1 or 2; its scry almost never triggers.
cards.Island: Basic blue source; it enables Sulfur Falls, Glacial Fortress and Radiant Summit.
cards.Plains: Basic white source; it enables Glacial Fortress, Clifftop Retreat and Radiant Summit.
cards.Mountain: Basic red source; it enables Sulfur Falls, Clifftop Retreat and Radiant Summit.
